problem_text:
A logistics company needs to schedule 6 delivery trucks to visit 6 distribution centers in a specific sequence.

Each truck must follow a predetermined route, represented as pairs (Center, Unloading time), where each pair specifies the distribution center to visit and the time required for unloading. The order of pairs indicates the strict sequence in which the centers must be visited.

Truck routes:
* T1 follows: (C6, 7) → (C1, 5) → (C3, 7) → (C4, 4) → (C2, 6) → (C5, 3)
* T2 follows: (C2, 10) → (C1, 7) → (C3, 8) → (C5, 2) → (C4, 2) → (C6, 7)
* T3 follows: (C5, 3) → (C6, 4) → (C2, 1) → (C1, 9) → (C3, 3) → (C4, 8)
* T4 follows: (C3, 7) → (C5, 5) → (C6, 3) → (C4, 6) → (C2, 9) → (C1, 6)
* T5 follows: (C5, 7) → (C2, 6) → (C4, 7) → (C3, 8) → (C6, 9) → (C1, 5)
* T6 follows: (C4, 1) → (C6, 10) → (C1, 10) → (C3, 9) → (C5, 2) → (C2, 4)

Each unloading operation must proceed without interruption once it begins, and each distribution center can only accommodate one truck at a time for unloading. The objective is to determine the optimal schedule for all unloading operations at the centers so that the total completion time for all trucks is minimized.
